items.followUp: State the number of electrons in the stable outer shell of neon and in the first shell of helium.

rubric.why: The duplet rule describes stability when the first shell is complete.
rubric.description: States that a duplet is two electrons in the first shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the duplet as two electrons in the first shell.

rubric.why: The octet rule describes stability with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: States that an octet is eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the octet as eight outermost-shell electrons.

modelAnswer: Duplet rule: an atom becomes stable when it has two electrons in its first shell.
Octet rule: an atom becomes stable when it has eight electrons in its outermost shell.

items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond forms by sharing one pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Defines a single covalent bond as sharing one pair of electrons between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one pair of electrons is shared.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates a single covalent bond.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example, such as H₂, Cl₂, HCl or CH₄.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct example.

modelAnswer: A single covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one pair of electrons.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and explain how it differs from condensation.

rubric.why: Vapour pressure is a pressure exerted by vapour, not a change of state.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour above its liquid at a given temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the pressure exerted by vapour.

rubric.why: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid.
rubric.description: Defines condensation as the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the gas-to-liquid change.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour above its liquid at a given temperature.
Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid.

items.followUp: Name a non-polar solvent that dissolves iodine, and state the general rule for solubility of covalent substances.

rubric.why: Non-polar covalent substances generally dissolve in non-polar solvents.
rubric.description: Identifies non-polar solvents as the solvents in which non-polar covalent substances dissolve.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying non-polar solvents.

rubric.why: A valid example completes the response.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a non-polar solvent, such as benzene or carbon tetrachloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any suitable example.

modelAnswer: Non-polar covalent substances are soluble in non-polar solvents.

items.followUp: Why does water have a higher boiling point than expected for its small molecular mass?

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding is the intermolecular attraction responsible for the effect.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonding between molecules as the cause of the physical-property effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming hydrogen bonding.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding increases properties such as water's boiling point and surface tension.
rubric.description: States an affected physical property and gives water as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct property with water as the example.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding between molecules affects physical properties by increasing the boiling point and surface tension.
For example, water has a high boiling point because of hydrogen bonding.

items.followUp: What particles carry electric current through an electrolyte in solution?

rubric.why: An electrolyte is identified by its ability to conduct electricity when mobile ions are present.
rubric.description: Defines electrolytes as substances that conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an electrolyte conducts electricity in solution or when molten.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows understanding of the term.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of an electrolyte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid example.

modelAnswer: Electrolytes are substances that conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.

items.followUp: Write the balanced chemical equation for chlorine reacting with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: The reactants in the reaction are chlorine and water.
rubric.description: Writes chlorine and water as the reactants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the reactants.

rubric.why: Chlorine reacts reversibly with water to form hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid.
rubric.description: Gives the correct products, hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid.

rubric.why: Platinum is used to make jewellery and ornaments.
rubric.description: Gives jewellery or ornaments as one use of platinum.

rubric.why: Platinum is used as a catalyst, including in catalytic converters and hydrogenation reactions.
rubric.description: Gives a catalytic use of platinum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid catalytic use.

modelAnswer: Platinum is used to make jewellery and ornaments.
It is used as a catalyst, for example in catalytic converters.
